A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Perception Magnifier work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary material support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, qualitative examples, and experiments with LLaVA and Shikra.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds MMHal-Bench evaluation, a DualView control, and measured inference runtimes.

M1.justification: PM retains its attention aggregation, iterative masking, heatmap processing, resampling, and decoding procedure. Specifying last-generated-token attention and 2-means clustering clarifies implementation; DualView is an experimental alternative rather than a replacement for PM.

E1.justification: v4 adds MMHal-Bench's 96 image-question pairs spanning eight question types and twelve object categories, extending open-ended hallucination evaluation. MME, POPE, and both LLaVA-Bench subsets remain.

E2.justification: Table 4(b) adds DualView as a comparison method. ViCrop-P, previously discussed but excluded from benchmarking, appears in the new runtime comparison in Figure 6. Comparator membership in the retained benchmark tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: v4 adds MMHal-Bench's GPT-4-based overall-score and hallucination-rate protocol, a dual-image input control, and average per-question runtime measurements. Existing model configurations, hyperparameters, beam size, and LLaVA-Bench evaluation prompts remain unchanged. The timing workload is not specified.

E4.justification: New analyses test original-plus-magnified inputs through DualView, iterative refinement on MMHal-Bench, and inference cost. Existing component ablations, map comparisons, hyperparameter sensitivity, and qualitative failure examples remain; the hyperparameter analysis moves to Appendix F.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new average-runtime plot adds a measured outcome without introducing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All pre-existing table values remain unchanged. Table 4 adds DualView's MME total of 650.00 versus PM's retained 683.33. New Figure 3 plots PM at approximately 2.18 overall score and 0.62 hallucination rate, versus PAI at 2.20 and 0.63; Figure 6 adds runtimes. POPE prose changes from winning all splits to most, matching the retained results more accurately.

T1.justification: The method overview corrects next-step conditioning from previous probability logits to previously generated tokens. This changes the stated mathematical relation rather than merely renaming an equivalent variable. Numbered Equations (1)-(4) and Algorithm 1 otherwise retain the same mathematics; no proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the claims of adaptive attention-guided magnification, improved hallucination mitigation, and preserved reasoning capabilities. The additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v4 proposes additional explanations for weaker results involving primary-object questions, response verbosity, world knowledge, and language-prior bias. It interprets measured runtime as a cost-quality tradeoff and recommends full PM for latency-tolerant settings. Existing distortion, caching, and compatibility limitations largely remain.

D1.justification: v4 adds a repository link, specifies last-token attention and 2-means clustering, reports approximately 24 GPU hours for all benchmarks, and supplies artifact-license information. Previously reported hardware, software versions, and principal hyperparameters are retained; these additions mainly improve disclosure.

R1.justification: v4 adds literature on preference optimization, context-aware decoding, attention intervention, and multi-path reasoning, plus references supporting MMHal-Bench and benchmark exclusions. Existing cited works remain, including IBD under updated publication metadata. PM's central positioning against decoding and cropping approaches is retained.

P1.justification: v4 numbers sections, letters appendices, relocates hyperparameter discussion, adds limitations and disclosure sections, and locally revises explanatory paragraphs. The overall narrative persists. Editing regressions include duplicated chair-example text and an unfinished DualView sentence.

P2.justification: The entire document changes from Letter-sized pages with approximately 10-point body text to A4 with approximately 11-point text, narrower columns, and different heading and citation styling. Figure 2's arrows and labels are revised, two plots are added, Table 4 gains a row, and existing displays are resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens supporting evidence through MMHal-Bench and the DualView control, and quantifies an efficiency limitation that v3 discussed qualitatively. Clearer implementation disclosures and POPE wording improve reproducibility and accuracy. These benefits outweigh local editorial regressions, although unspecified timing conditions and the unfinished DualView discussion limit the gain.
